definitions.full: H7497. Rapha II. רְפָאִים proper name, of a people old race of giants (perhaps = I. ׳ר , as extinct and powerless ; see especially WRS in Dr Deut 2:11 ; or as shadowy, vaguely known, Schw ZAW xviii (1898), 127 ff. see also Sta l.c .); — ancient inhabitants of Canaan [west of Jordan?], Gen 15:20 ; Josh 17:15 (JE), compare 1Chr 20:4 (see II. רָפָה above); hence ר ׳עֶמֶמק , plain south of Jerusalem 2Sam 5:18 , 22 ; 23:13 ; 1Chr 11:15 ; 14:9 ; Isa 17:5 ; Josh 15:8 ; 18:16 (P); ׳ר east of Jordan Deut 2:11 (|| עֲנָקִים ; tall, compare 2:10 ), 2:20 (|| id. ; tall; = Zamzummim); in Bashan, Gen 14:5 , Og the last of them Deut 3:11 (of huge size), Josh 12:4 ; 13:12 (D); ר ׳אֶרֶץ Deut 2:20 ; 3:13 . ᵐ5 Ραφαειν[μ] ; οἱ γίγαντες Gen 14:5 4 t.; τῶν Τιτάνων 2Sam 5:18 , 22 + ( ᵐ5 L ) 23:13 . רִפוֺת see רִיפָה below ריף . p. 937.
definitions.rootNote: or רָפָה ; from 7495 in the sense of invigorating;

Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest, and clear land for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”

The border went down to the farthest part of the mountain that lies before the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the valley of Rephaim northward. It went down to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite southward, and went down to En Rogel.

and Ishbibenob, who was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze in weight, he being armed with a new sword, thought he would kill David.

There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had six fingers on every hand, and six toes on every foot, twenty four in count; and he also was born to the giant.
These four were born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
